item.title: The path back to 2 % has become less comfortable

rating.summary: Bank of Finland Board Member Tuomas Välimäki describes the euro area inflation outlook as 'less comfortable' following a renewed energy shock that has pushed headline inflation to 3.8%, while noting that underlying inflation, wages, and long-term expectations remain broadly stable. He explains the ECB's decision to hold rates unchanged at its October meeting, emphasizing a meeting-by-meeting, data-dependent approach given the stagflationary nature of the shock. He acknowledges upside inflation risks but stresses the need to distinguish between transitory headline effects and persistent inflation dynamics.
rating.stance_rationale: The speech is balanced, neither signaling imminent rate hikes nor cuts; the ECB held rates and Välimäki stresses caution and data dependence in both directions, with the energy shock creating offsetting pressures on inflation and growth that prevent a clear directional lean.
key_quotes: the renewed energy shock has made the outlook more uncomfortable, but it has not – at least so far – fundamentally changed the underlying inflation picture
pre-committing to a rate path would create a false sense of precision
